workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Windows: portfolio real-tool scenario fails — node:sqlite cannot open the 267-char authority path (MAX_PATH); a second host-dependent layer behind it
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(sqlite_authority_store): surface underlying SQLite error in status. Target files: loopx/control_plane/coordination/sqlite_authority_store.ts. The issue was that SQLite errors (like "unable to open database file" due to path length limits on Windows) were being collapsed into a generic "lock contention" message in the `readFailure` function. This made it difficult to diagnose the root cause of database opening failures. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/8459)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Host recovery I/O uses the locale codec, silently dropping non-ASCII Antigravity Stop events on cp936
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(runtime): pin UTF-8 on host recovery I/O. Target files: loopx/agy_goal_mode/host_runtime.py, loopx/hosts/managed_service_runtime.py, tests/test_antigravity_host_runtime.py. Latest `main` fails its two package-wide UTF-8 guards, so every pull request inherits a red Python test lane; the same omissions silently discard non-ASCII Antigravity Stop recovery on cp936 Windows and can block managed-runtime journal recovery. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/8031)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: native Windows Codex App settlement plans emit a POSIX-only Turn reference
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(quota): render host-native settlement Turn references. Target files: loopx/control_plane/quota/effect_program.py, tests/control_plane/test_quota_settlement.py. Native Windows Codex App admission can block every no-Turn settlement after the work succeeds because the returned plan contains a POSIX-only Turn placeholder that PowerShell forwards as an empty argument; this affects the supported native Windows App journey and the validation, writeback, spend, and closeout steps generated from it. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/7823)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: native Windows --write-worktree scoped observation rejects every in-scope path
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(leases): accept scoped native Windows worktree paths. Target files: loopx/control_plane/work_items/task_lease_workspace.ts, .github/workflows/python-tests.yml, scripts/ci/test_windows_lane_coverage.py. Native Windows `--write-worktree` observation rejected existing in-scope entries because `realpath()` returns native separators while the containment test appended a literal slash.
